newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.
newsitem.headline: Asian dollar deposits quietly steady in late trade.

text.p: Asian dollar deposit rates were quietly steady in bland trade, with most people sidelined ahead of tonight's release of the U.S April employment and March leading indicators reports, dealers said on Friday.

In the April employment report, non-farm payrolls are forecast to be around 211,000 compared with 175,000 reported in March. The unemployment rate is expected to be unchanged from March's 5.2 percent.
March leading indicators are expected to show a gain of 0.2 percent against February's 0.5 percent increase.

"Rates were steady to easier in the morning on some position adjustments. All eyes are now on tonight's release of the employment report and leading indicators figures, but most people have squared their positions for the weekend," a local dealer said.
"The numbers have also been built into the market, so unless the figures are way off market expectations, I don't think there will be much impact," he said.
In day-to-day rates, weekend slipped 1/8 percentage point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent and Monday/Tuesday eased 1/16 point to 5-9/16 5-7/16 percent.
Week-fixed was unchanged from Wednesday's 5-5/8 5-1/2 percent.

Among longer dates, two-months was unchanged at 5-3/4 5-5/8 percent, four-months eased 1/16 point to 5-13/16 5-11/16, six-months was unchanged at 6 5-7/8 and twelve-months eased 1/16 point to 6-1/4 6-1/8 percent.
